title: Using Caching for Scalability
description: Understand caching layers, invalidation strategies, and tradeoffs to reduce load and improve scalability.

data.text: Caching stores frequently accessed data closer to the consumer so expensive operations—database queries, API calls, or computation—are avoided. Good caching reduces load, lowers latency, and increases effective capacity without scaling infrastructure.
Caches can exist at multiple points in the stack. Each layer serves different access patterns and has different performance characteristics.

items: CDN: caches static assets and edge-cached API responses near users
Application cache: in-memory caches like Redis or Memcached for hot data
Database cache: query caches or buffer pools inside the database engine
Client cache: browser cache, local storage, or service workers

rows: App reads cache, falls back to DB, then writes cache
Writes go to cache and DB together
Writes hit cache only; DB updates later

data.text: The hardest part of caching is deciding when to remove or update cached data. Stale cache entries can mislead users or break correctness. Common patterns include time-to-live expiration, event-driven invalidation, and versioned cache keys.

data.title: Warning
data.text: Avoid caching without an invalidation plan. Incorrect stale data is often worse than a cache miss.

data.caption: Multi-layer caching from CDN to application cache
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    User --> CDN[CDN / Edge Cache]
    CDN -->|miss| App[App Server]
    App -->|miss| Redis[Redis Cache]
    Redis -->|miss| DB[(Database)]
    DB -->|populate| Redis
    Redis -->|populate| App
    App -->|populate| CDN

items.text: Define TTLs or invalidation events for every cached dataset
items.hint: Never cache indefinitely without a refresh plan.
Aim for 80%+ hit ratios on hot caches.

items.text: Avoid caching user-specific data in shared caches without key separation
Plan for cache failures: your app should continue working if the cache is down
Use versioned keys to invalidate broad datasets cleanly

data.title: Summary
points: Caching reduces load but adds complexity.
Choose strategy based on read/write patterns and consistency needs.
Layer caches for maximum impact: CDN, app cache, DB buffer pool.
data.takeaway: Caching is a multiplier for performance, not a replacement for sound data architecture.
